defects.description: No edges show customers or adjusters signing in to their Cognito pools, and Lambda functions have no explicit log or metric edges to CloudWatch.

Tamper-evidence relies on CloudTrail log file validation and S3 versioning; S3 Object Lock is not specified for the audit bucket. Step Functions execution history is the main step-level audit source but is not called out as one.
Two Cognito user pools with two authorizers on a REST API add some complexity compared with one pool and groups.

reviews.summary: Complete and well-reasoned design: Step Functions task-token wait with timeout handling, idempotent starts, EventBridge-to-SQS failure surfacing, CloudTrail with validation to a KMS-encrypted audit bucket, CMKs, and WAF on a REST API.

defects.description: CloudTrail is described as an immutable compliance-grade audit log, but the design has no S3 destination bucket, log file validation, or retention. Its only edge goes to CloudWatch. Without a trail delivering to S3, only the 90-day Event history is available, so the long-term audit requirement is not met.
Application audit records in the shared DynamoDB table are called immutable, but nothing enforces immutability (for example restrictive IAM or a write-once pattern).
There is no explicit DLQ or failure-event routing for failed executions. Only CloudWatch alarms are mentioned.

The automated-checks Lambda is invoked with the task token and also stores it. That conflates the checks step with the 14-day wait, so a Lambda failure after the token is stored complicates retries. The Intake-to-S3 presigned URL edge is labeled invoke, which is semantically loose.
There is no WAF, which is acceptable with an HTTP API but leaves the public intake endpoint less protected. All encryption uses AWS-managed keys.

reviews.summary: Workable serverless workflow with Step Functions task-token wait and single Cognito pool with groups, but the audit story is weak because CloudTrail has no durable store and failure handling is thinner.
